blocks.text: However that may be, the sacred writer passes from voice and sound to military order, and says in verse 5: It is like a strong people, set in array for battle. 6. Before its face the peoples shall tremble; all faces shall gather paleness. 7. They shall run like mighty soldiers; like men of war they shall climb the wall. Each shall march in his own ways, and they shall not break their paths. 8. And one shall not thrust another; each shall march in his own track. Even falling upon the sword they shall not be wounded. 9. They shall go through the city, they shall climb up into the houses, they shall enter in at the very windows like a thief.] In these words it must first be noted that this army, whatever it is, is now called not a people but like a people. So when the Prophet [col. 477] [III, 311] above ^{b)} called it a nation and a people, he was speaking metaphorically, calling a people those forces which are not really a people, but are like a people set in array for battle. Of the same kind is his addition that they run like mighty soldiers and climb the wall like men of war, so that no one should imagine real soldiers and warriors here. But although they are not soldiers, they are nevertheless rightly compared with real soldiers: 1. on account of their number and strength. It is like a strong people. Jerome: What is more innumerable and stronger than locusts, which human industry cannot resist? Cyril: Χρῆμα ἄμαχον, καὶ δυσκαταγώνιστον παντελῶς ἀνθρώποις, βρούχου καὶ ἀκρίδος ἐμβολή· [Chrēma amachon, kai dyskatagōniston pantelōs anthrōpois, brouchou kai akridos embolē] The onslaught of the bruchus and the locust is invincible, and utterly insuperable for men. Pisides describes their manner of fighting thus:

Τὸ πτηνὸν ὅπλον εἰς ἀνάμνησιν φόβου, [To ptēnon hoplon eis anamnēsin phobou,] Βέλος νεφῶδες ἐξ ἀδήλου τοξότου, [Belos nephōdes ex adēlou toxotou,] Λόγχην ἑτοίμην, αὐτοκίνητον δόρυ, [Lonchēn hetoimēn, autokinēton dory,] Πυκνὴν φάλαγγα, μυριόστομον ξίφος, [Pyknēn phalanga, myriostomon xiphos,] Πηδητικὴν ἔπαλξιν ἀστάτου μάχης. [Pēdētikēn epalxin astatou machēs.] Οὐχ ἵσταται γὰρ, ἀλλὰ πλήττει, καὶ τρέχει, [Ouch histatai gar, alla plēttei, kai trechei,] Ἕρπουσα πορθεῖ, καὶ κλονεῖ πτερουμένη. [Herpousa porthei, kai klonei pteroumenē.] Δοκεῖ δὲ φεύγειν, καὶ παλίνδρομος μένει. [Dokei de pheugein, kai palindromos menei.]
